I give up. I did not write a proof, and the file is unchanged.

The statement is true: the Putnam 2021 A6 answer is "yes, P(2) is composite." The difficulty is that I don't have a complete argument I could formalize. Two steps I checked are sound. Every complex root z of P satisfies |z| < 2, by a Cauchy-type bound. Since P has 0/1 coefficients, P(2) ≥ 1, so P(2) ≠ 0 and, when P is nonconstant, P(2) ≠ 1. The missing piece is the step that rules out P(2) being prime, which requires either the official argument or a substitute I haven't found. Even with that, the formalization would need Lean infrastructure for root bounds and factor analysis that is well beyond this attempt.
